Sanjay — thanks for the clear asks and the spreadsheet. High level first, then an annotated example you can paste into your SOW.

High-level:
- Committed anchor (Reserved): you get a monthly anchor of X units (you bought 10). Anchor units consume first; bursts beyond the anchor are billed at the pay-as-you-go (PAYG) rate. Rounding happens at the invoice line item level depending on the SKU: for token SKUs we round up to the nearest billing quantum (100 tokens) per call unless the call is part of an active session bucket for which session aggregation applies.
- Ephemeral / Transactional: each request is independently rounded to the call quantum. If your invoice falls below a low-volume safety minimum, our invoicing layer applies the daily minimum (1,000 tokens/day) unless you opt out through a pilot waiver.
- KV/prefix reuse: when the runtime detects prefix reuse it emits a KV-credit token line which is subtracted on the invoice. We typically show this as a negative line item labeled "KV reuse credit". Example numbers below.

Annotated example (paste-ready):
- Raw call: prompt 1,800 tokens + response 2,600 tokens = 4,400 raw tokens
- Streaming fragmentation: call split into 3 chunks (client sent incremental); the billing engine keeps the call-level token total and applies rounding once per completed request = 4,400 tokens
- Call quantum rounding: round up to nearest 100 => 4,400 stays 4,400 (already at quantum)
- Anchor consumption: anchor 10 units cover up to 10,000 tokens/minute of sustained throughput (opaque to SOW). This single call consumes 4,400 tokens from anchored pool (no PAYG charge).
- KV reuse (60%): assume 60% of prompt tokens were prefix matches => KV credit = 1,080 tokens (60% of 1,800) credited back at token rate
- Invoice lines:
  - Anchor allocation: consumed 4,400 tokens (no itemized charge; included in monthly anchor)
  - PAYG token usage: 0 tokens
  - KV reuse credit: -1,080 tokens (negative line at token rate)
  - Net billable tokens for this call (if not fully covered by anchor): 3,320 tokens

Month-end true-up note: if you exceeded anchor capacity during spikes, true-up compares aggregated monthly consumption vs anchor allowance. We prorate by day for mid-month upgrades. Credits from KV reuse are applied before computing PAYG true-up. The only exceptions you might see: model variant fallbacks (runtime switches to a cheaper variant automatically) which are logged but charged at the fallback SKU unless covered by a negotiated fallback clause.

I'll attach an example invoice row in a follow-up with numeric rates plugged in. Vanessa / Karthik — can you add the numeric rates and a sample invoice with the attached spreadsheet?

Sample invoice rows (USD):

- Example call (from Hannah): raw tokens 4,400 -> after KV credit -1,080 = net 3,320 tokens
- Token rate (PAYG): $0.00008 / token => call PAYG value = $0.266 (only if outside anchor)

- Daily minimum for ephemeral pilot: 1,000 tokens/day -> $0.08/day if pilot uses <1,000 tokens; invoice shows minimum line if applicable.

Exception policy:
- If a call spans two different runtime model variants due to an automatic fallback, we split the call billing by variant at the fragment boundary and apply respective rates. This is rare and flagged in the billing trace.

Recommended SOW paragraph for procurement (one-liner):
"Billable usage is computed per completed request, rounded to the configured token quantum (100 tokens), with KV/prefix reuse applied as credits. Reserved anchors consume billable units first; overage is billed PAYG. A low-volume daily minimum of 1,000 tokens applies to ephemeral pilots unless waived in writing"
